assessment: The incumbent supplies an assembled organizer, checks the order, and offers layout guidance. Repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, so near-target workshop performance occurs under some conditions. Mixed batches contained every extreme delay, but layout complexity and switching are confounded. Missing/incorrect-part reports and short-partition questions indicate distinct fulfillment and comprehension concerns; their causes remain unestablished. A concrete limit on a simple dimensional explanation is D2-O5: widths overlap between first-attempt and retry parts. Width alone therefore does not separate those groups. Neither zero recorded damage claims nor the small unpacking session establishes pilot success.

openings.claim: Switching between order requirements may increase selection/checking time and component errors; order-specific temporary kits may reduce that burden.
openings.delta: Replace shared-bin selection during assembly with a counted tray of the exact ordered parts and exterior color, using reusable board dividers.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts, temporary kits reduce total preparation-through-packing time and discrepancies, especially after layout switches. Unchanged selection time with persistent insertion delays weakens this account.
openings.probe: Use five reusable sample sets in counterbalanced mixed and grouped sequences across both workers. Compare current selection with counted kits; time kit preparation, selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, and audit contents against each order. Treat repetitions as diagnostic, not independent pilot orders.
assumptions: Kit preparation is included in total labor.
Reusable supplies fit the initial budget; implementation must meet the recurring-cost cap and fixed date.

openings.claim: The generic three-layout diagram may leave the short partition's ordered position ambiguous; an order-specific diagram may improve unaided arrangement.
openings.delta: Show the selected arrangement with the short partition and its insertion orientation clearly identified.
openings.prediction: Correct first placement and fewer location questions support a comprehension benefit. Correct identification followed by repeated insertion failures instead indicates a remaining mechanical limitation.
openings.probe: Allocate ten remaining samples and ten participants between existing and revised diagrams, balancing layout complexity. Record first placement, insertion retries, unaided completion and elapsed time. This small comparison screens the hypothesis; verify the 90% threshold in the pilot.
assumptions: Diagram replacement fits cost and delivery limits.
Parts, footprint, capacity, removability, ordered compartment counts and exterior colors remain as specified.
